wins: Established comprehensive reconnaissance by scanning all accessible subnets and documenting available services, providing a solid insight baseline.
Triggered advanced service enumeration (e.g., HTTP/SMB) that captured detailed version banners for later exploitation planning.
fails: Failed to maintain a foothold or achieve objective despite multiple pivot attempts, resulting in 0% success rate.
High mentor call volume (15) indicates repeated uncertainty around next-step decisions, slowing momentum.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance depth was strong, but the inability to translate findings into exploitation/persistence caused the run to fall short of objectives.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Exploitation attempts halted due to missing valid credentials for SMB/HTTP authentication.
Unable to escalate privileges after initial shell access because post-exploitation modules were not deployed.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with targeted nmap scripts and manual banner parsing

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP service responds with outdated server header
skill_cards.then_action: Invoke nikto/gobuster for directory brute-force and script-based vulnerability identification

skill_cards.if_condition: When valid SMB share credentials are discovered during enumeration
skill_cards.then_action: Map shares with smbclient and harvest potential scripts/data for lateral movement

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in reconnaissance phase for SSH services and consistent banner information gathering
HTTP vulnerability enumeration consistently triggered additional actionable leads

next_experiments.title: Targeted credential harvesting for SMB/HTTP
next_experiments.description: Deploy credential stuffing (Hydra) and password spraying based on observed user lists to unlock authenticated SMB and HTTP entry points.

next_experiments.title: Post-exploitation automation
next_experiments.description: Integrate automated privilege escalation and persistence scripts (e.g., WinPEAS, PowerUp) immediately after shell acquisition to avoid losing foothold.

next_experiments.title: Pivot via exposed internal services
next_experiments.description: Use captured service banners to prioritize lateral movement toward internal admin interfaces (e.g., RDP, MSSQL) with targeted exploits.
